# rawsock — spec

## Maturity

**Grade:** 2 · S2 E1 A2 H1 P2 · limited by scope (parity), audit (src it ran over not recorded), performance (fastest in the field not measured) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** parity — libpcap 1.10.6 on Linux (live capture incl. an opt-in `TPACKET_V3` or `TPACKET_V2` ring; the `pcap_compile` filter language incl. `vlan`, offline and in the live ancillary form alone and combined, over Ethernet, Linux cooked v1 and v2, raw IP, DLT_NULL, DLT_LOOP and DLT_PPP; classic pcap + pcapng savefiles). Also `inbound`, `outbound`, `ifindex`, `pppoed`, and `mpls` / `pppoes`, alone and combined with IP, IPv6 and what rides on them (`mpls` as a label stack, `pppoes` once); also `geneve [vni]` (Ethernet); every other libpcap feature a Linux user would notice is rejected with a reason or deferred (see "What is deliberately not done" and Backlog) (surveyed 2026-11-04)

**Audit:** review 2026-10-04 · mutation 2026-10-04 (39/41, 2 eq) · src ?

**Hardening:** fuzz 2026-11-04 (200,000 runs per harness, ReleaseSafe test binary run directly in `unshare -rn`, `runs=200000` lines seen on all 10 harnesses, all 144 tests, final code; the filter harness drives every link and both vlan forms and reaches the run-time vlan form and the new links, asserted) · ct n/a — raw sockets (keyword review, 2026-10-07) · panic 2026-10-30 (sweep + blind review: filter compile stack overflow on long and/or chains (leaf cap; a loop for left-deep chains and parser nesting 16 since 2026-11-04, the deepest accepted inputs compile in a 64 KiB stack, tested), run jump saturation, cmsg/pcap totality, ifname NUL; delta audit 32/36 + 4 eq); 2026-11-04 sweep entries for every link, both vlan forms, `runLive` and `Link.fromDlt`

**Performance:** ref 0.92× libpcap 1.10.6 source build (worst row `filter_run`, 21 rounds, final code, wall time, a host with other jobs on it, spreads 12-50 %; 0.90× with `-Djcc-safe` on both sides; `compile` 0.65×, `filter_run_lp` 0.82×; user instructions, stable where wall time is not: `compile` 0.72×, `filter_run` 0.95×; savefile rows 0.13, 0.53, 0.22× are libpcap's stdio plus a per-packet copy, different work, no speed claim; other runs of this code put `filter_run` at 0.91-1.03×) · fastest ? (measured 2026-11-04). On the filter and compile rows no other implementation has the language, so there is nothing to be fastest against; on the savefile rows gopacket pcapgo is slower than ours and the Rust `pcap-file` crate, an info row, is equal within the noise. **P2 rests on the SOURCE build** (libpcap from the pinned tag, CMake `Release` `-O3`, static, built by the coordinator, `LIBPCAP=…/libpcap.a`). The distro build of the same source (libpcap.so.0.8) is not another implementation, and it is not settled: `filter_run` 1.14× at spread 8.8 % in one run, 1.03× at spread 57 % in another; `filter.run` did not change between them, so the tighter 1.14× is the better estimate. Ours executes fewer instructions (0.93×) at a lower IPC (1.61 against 2.04); unprofiled, Backlog has the `perf` commands.

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** yes

Design + threat notes for auditors. Usage: see ./README.md. Attribution/provenance: original work of
the zig-libs authors (MIT).

**Where we are ahead:** the only pure-Zig, libc-free AF_PACKET capture **and** inject path we found: in-kernel classic-BPF attach, promiscuous mode, kernel drop counters (`Socket.stats`), the 802.1Q tag recovered through `PACKET_AUXDATA` (`Frame.vlan_tci` — the kernel strips it before a tap sees the frame, so a naive capture loses it), a `sockaddr_ll` decoder, an ARP codec, and real-segment ARP/IPv4 goldens from a veth pair. **Where we are behind** (re-checked 2026-11-04): no `recvmmsg` batching; no 802.11 / PPP-savefile link layers (Backlog); the generated filter code is unoptimised (longer than libpcap's; the same verdicts except the known `ip and vlan` deviation); no host-name/service-name resolution; Linux only by design (→ "What is deliberately not done"). Built since the survey: `filter.compile`/`run` (2026-10-04; on 2026-11-03 IPv6 `host`/`net`, bare `host`/`net`, `portrange`, `less`/`greater`/`len`, `broadcast`/`multicast`, `proto[off:size] & mask RELOP n` offset expressions, `arp`/`rarp host`), `pcap` savefiles, `pcapng` reader and writer (2026-11-03), `Frame.timestamp_ns`, `Socket.joinFanout`.

## Design & invariants

- **Linux AF_PACKET capture + inject, no libpcap, no libc.** Open a `SOCK_RAW` capture socket for
  one EtherType (or every frame, `eth_p.all`), decode the kernel's `sockaddr_ll` into a typed
  `Frame`, attach an in-kernel classic-BPF filter, toggle promiscuous mode, and cook-inject frames
  on a named interface (a `SOCK_DGRAM` socket where the kernel builds the Ethernet header) or
  transmit a complete frame on the raw socket (`sendRaw`). Original work of the zig-libs authors
  (MIT), starting from a minimal receive-only ~25-LOC core (`openPacketCapture`/`ifNameOf`); the
  send path, `SO_ATTACH_FILTER` filtering, `PACKET_ADD_MEMBERSHIP` promiscuous mode, interface
  lookup by name/index (there is no listing), and the typed `Frame`/`LinkAddr`/`EthHeader` decode are new construction. Wire layout
  clean-room from `packet(7)`, Linux UAPI headers (`<linux/if_packet.h>`, `<linux/if_ether.h>`,
  `<linux/filter.h>`), IEEE 802.3/802.1AB, and ARP, with EtherStruct (BSD-2-Clause) consulted
  only as a header-field-order cross-check (no source copied). libpcap's
  source was read only on 2026-11-04 for the questions in "Compared with"; nothing was ported.
- **Pure helpers need no socket/privilege:** `EthHeader.parse`/`.write`, `parseHwaddr`/
  `formatHwaddr` (MAC ⇄ `"aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff"`), `LinkAddr.fromSockaddr` (the `sockaddr_ll` decode
  `recv` uses), `bpf`/`etherTypeFilter` (classic-BPF program builder; wire-format `BpfInsn` is 8
  bytes, asserted), `arp.buildRequest`/`arp.parseReply` (addresses surface as `netaddr.Ip`).
- **Raw errno syscalls, no libc:** all socket/ioctl calls go through `std.os.linux` directly, a
  conscious ceiling shared with `icmp`/`netlink`. Kernel struct sizes (`sockaddr_ll`, `BpfInsn`) are
  asserted in tests against the documented ABI.
- **Concurrency:** reentrant — no shared state; one `Socket` per thread/loop.

## Filter compiler, savefiles, timestamps, fanout

**`filter.compile`.** Working memory: an 8 KiB stack buffer, then a per-call arena on the caller's allocator (a long filter past 8 KiB on `std.heap.smp_allocator` is the shape that grows it without bound); `filter.compileInto(out, scratch, expr, opts)` touches no allocator at all (caller-owned scratch and output, `OutOfMemory` when either is too small). Recursive descent over the language in `src/filter.zig`'s header (parentheses and `not` nest at most `Parser.max_depth` = 16; a left-deep and/or chain is walked by a loop, so the deepest accepted input compiles in a 64 KiB stack, tested), an AST of single comparisons (`load [x+]off | #pktlen; [and #mask;] jeq|jset|jge|jgt #k`), and code
generation by true/false labels: `a and b` sends `a`'s false edge to the failure label and its true
edge to `b`; `or` mirrors it; `not` swaps the labels. Every jump is forward, so the program is a
DAG; a jump longer than 255 instructions goes through a `ja` stub (as libpcap does), never a truncated jump, and a program past `BPF_MAXINSNS` (`max_insns`, 4096) is
`error.FilterTooComplex`. `and` and `or` have equal precedence and associate left to right (`man pcap-filter`; `tcpdump -d 'tcp or udp and port 53'` compiles to `(tcp or udp) and port 53`). The meaning of each primitive was read off
libpcap's own output (`tcpdump -d`, black box): IPv4 ports require fragment offset 0 and locate
the header with `ldxb 4*([14]&0xf)`; IPv6 transport protocols also match through a fragment
header (44) but IPv6 ports do not walk extension headers; `port` alone is tcp|udp|sctp; `icmp` is
IPv4 only. libpcap's "non-network bits set" refusal for `net` is mirrored.

**`filter.run`.** The kernel's classic-BPF semantics: an out-of-bounds load, a division by zero,
an opcode the kernel would refuse at attach time or running off the end returns 0 (drop); a scratch slot nothing stored to reads 0. One `switch` over the full opcode. It terminates in at most `prog.len`
steps because every instruction advances and no jump goes backwards. Where the kernel and libpcap's userspace interpreter differ, `run` follows the kernel: `X + k` wraps in 32 bits (`ldx #0xffffffff; ld [x+2]` loads offset 1; libpcap's drops), a register shift count is masked to five bits (`1 << X` with X = 32 is 1; `A <<= X` with X >= 32 is undefined behaviour in libpcap's C), and division or modulus by X = 0 drops the frame. A constant shift of 32 or more, `ld M[k]` before any store and an offset in `[-0x1000, 0)` that is not an `SKF_AD_*` word are refused by the kernel at attach time; `validate` is that attach-time check list and every program `compile` emits passes it. `run` has a frame and nothing else, so a negative or ancillary load drops (`usesAncillary` says whether a program has one; `runLive` and `runLiveMeta` answer the vlan, packet-type and interface-index words from metadata).

**`pcapng`.** Reader: Section Header (either byte order, several sections), Interface Description (`if_tsresol` decimal up to 10^-18 and binary up to 2^-62, `if_tsoffset`, up to `max_interfaces` = 32 per section), Enhanced, Simple and the obsolete Packet Blocks; every other block type is skipped by its length. Every block length is checked (multiple of 4, framing, trailer equal, inside the input) before a slice is formed; an instant outside 64-bit nanoseconds is `BadTimestamp`, never wrapped. Writer: host byte order, one interface, `if_tsresol` 6 or 9, EPBs. Decisions checked against libpcap and Wireshark `capinfos`: a type-2 Packet Block is read by both (and here); a Simple Packet Block longer than its block is corrupt in both (`BadBlock`); `if_tsresol` with length other than 1 is refused by libpcap and accepted by Wireshark (refused here, `BadBlock`); a decimal resolution above 10^-18 or binary above 2^-62 is accepted by both with a meaningless time (`BadTimestamp` here: a documented difference); a packet naming an undeclared interface is an error in both (`BadInterface`); 33 interfaces are fine in both, while the reader here caps at `max_interfaces` because its table has no allocator (`TooManyInterfaces`).

**`pcap`.** The writer emits host byte order (as libpcap does); the reader takes either order and
µs or ns magic, and refuses a record longer than `max(snaplen, 262144)` (a corrupt length, not a
frame) or one past the end of the input, before forming any slice. A µs file stores a ns time
truncated, as libpcap does.


**Timestamps.** Best-effort (no new `OpenError`; the module's own example switches on that set
exhaustively, and so may a consumer): `SO_TIMESTAMPNS_NEW` (64-bit `__kernel_timespec` on every arch), falling back to
`SO_TIMESTAMPNS_OLD` on an older 64-bit kernel; the cmsg parser shares the bounded walk of the
`PACKET_AUXDATA` one and rejects a negative time, a nanosecond field ≥ 10⁹ and a u64 overflow.

**Fanout.** One `setsockopt(PACKET_FANOUT, group | (mode | flags) << 16)`; the kernel enforces that
every member agrees on mode and flags, and a test proves the defrag flag reaches it.

## Ring, kernel metadata, vlan, link types

- **`TPACKET_V3` ring (`src/ring.zig`).** Opt-in; typed `InitError` (`BadSize`, `AccessDenied`, `RingUnsupported`, `OutOfMemory`); kernel packet/drop/freeze counters (`Ring.stats`); hostile block headers are bounded (`Block.init` / `nextPacket`: an error ends the block); `Ring.release` identifies the held block by a ticket and its own memory, so a stale or forged `Block` is `WrongBlock`; block sizes 4 KiB..16 MiB x 2..1024 blocks, 256 MiB total checked in 64 bits; a second ring on one socket is refused. Throughput against `recv` and libpcap: `bench-rawsock -- ring`, figures on the card.
- **`TPACKET_V2` ring (`ring.RingV2`).** libpcap offers V1, V2 and V3 rings (V2 for kernels and drivers where V3's block retire timers misbehave): one `tpacket2_hdr` per frame, fixed-size slots (`OptionsV2`: block size, block count, frame size 64..block, multiple of 16), `next` / `release` hand one frame at a time. `FrameV2.packet` checks every header field against the frame's bounds (`BadBlock` costs that packet only, because the slots are fixed-size and the cursor never depends on the header), the `release` ticket rules are `Ring`'s, `stats` has no freeze counter (`freezes` stays 0). A `TPACKET_V1` ring is not built (V2 supersedes it in everything libpcap's V1 mode offers; the V2 header only adds the vlan words and nanosecond stamps).
- **Kernel-metadata and MPLS/PPPoE primitives.** `inbound`, `outbound` (`ldh [type]`, `SKF_AD_PKTTYPE`, 4 = outgoing) and `ifindex N` (`SKF_AD_IFINDEX`) are checked against `tcpdump -i lo -dd` programs (same verdicts under `filter.runLiveMeta` for packet types 0, 3, 4 and two interface indexes) and live on `lo` in a netns. `mpls [N]` and `pppoes [N]` test EtherType 0x8847 / 0x8864 and the label / session id, and, as in libpcap, everything written AFTER them moves (the same sequential shift as `vlan`: +4 for the label, +8 for the PPPoE header and the PPP protocol field): over MPLS `ip` / `ip6` are the label's bottom-of-stack bit and the version nibble (no EtherType test; the bare `host` drops its ARP forms; `arp`, `rarp` and `vlan` are refused as libpcap refuses them), over PPPoE the PPP protocol field in place of the EtherType (0x0021, 0x0057, 0x0281; `arp` stays 0x0806; MAC addresses and `multicast` are refused: the link type is PPP). A second `mpls` is the next label of the stack, as in libpcap (`mpls 5 or mpls 100`, `mpls and mpls`): no EtherType test, the previous label's bottom-of-stack bit must be clear, and everything after moves by 4 per label; `pppoes and mpls` shifts by 4 after the PPP protocol test (0x0281) and takes a label number, so `pppoes and mpls and mpls and ip` works. Checked by 108 expression rows against `tcpdump -r` over 19 frames (MPLS stacks of one to three labels, PPPoE sessions with and without MPLS, discovery, plain IP; `tools/gen_mpls_oracle.py`, `src/testdata/mpls_oracle.zig`). Refused here though libpcap builds them: `mpls and pppoes`, `pppoes` after `pppoes` with a session id, and the live ancillary `vlan` form around them; `ip and mpls` compiles to a program that never matches where libpcap's optimiser refuses it.
- **`geneve [vni]`.** libpcap's form (tcpdump 4.99 `-d`, 50 instructions): the outer frame is IPv4 (not a fragment) or IPv6 (next header UDP, no extension headers), UDP destination port 6081, Geneve version 0 and the VNI (at most 16777215, else `Syntax`); the option length (6 bits, in 4-byte words) locates the inner frame; scratch slot 0 = offset of the inner EtherType (the Geneve protocol type, or for an Ethernet payload 0x6558 the inner frame's own), slot 1 = the inner frame's first byte, slot 2 = its network header (14 bytes later for an Ethernet payload). Primitives written AFTER `geneve` (parse order, as with `vlan` and `mpls`) load through those slots: the EtherType via slot 0, network-layer fields via slot 2 (`ip`, `ip6`, `host`, `net`, ports, `tcp[..]`, `ip[..]`, `ip proto`, `arp`), link-header fields via slot 1 (`ether src` / `dst` / `host`, `multicast`, `broadcast`, `ether[..]`; false when the payload is not Ethernet, slots 1 and 2 equal). Primitives written before it test the OUTER frame (`ip and geneve`). Checked by 61 expression rows against `tcpdump -r` over 21 frames (IPv4 and IPv6 outer, Ethernet and bare IP payloads, options, VNIs, near misses: version 1, another port, a fragment; `tools/gen_geneve_oracle.py`, `src/testdata/geneve_oracle.zig`), the programs pass `validate` and the kernel's own checker on `lo` (netns lane). Differences: where a primitive after `geneve` can run on a frame that never ran it (`geneve or tcp`, `not geneve and ip`) libpcap leaves the slots uninitialised (the kernel refuses its program), here they are zero-initialised at the start; Ethernet links only; `geneve` together with `vlan`, `mpls`, `pppoes` or a second `geneve` is `UnsupportedExpression` (libpcap builds them). `pppoed` is built (EtherType 0x8863); `carp` is refused by libpcap itself as an ip proto name.
- **`vlan` in combination, both forms, with libpcap's shift.** The offline (in-packet) form and the live (ancillary, `Options.vlan_ancillary`) form are in the language header. The live form is checked against 42 programs libpcap compiles for a live Ethernet device (`src/testdata/vlan_live.zig`) through `filter.runLive`: the same verdicts over in-frame tags, kernel-stripped tags with priority bits, id 0 and QinQ. One expression differs on purpose: libpcap's own live program for `ip and vlan 5` accepts nothing (it jumps over the `ldh [vlan_tci]`), ours accepts the frame it names. A libpcap quirk ours repeats: a failed `vlan` test leaves the shift at 4 (see Limits). The alone form decides on the metadata alone, as libpcap does.
- **Link types.** `Options.link` = `.ethernet`, `.linux_sll`, `.linux_sll2`, `.raw`, `.bsd_null`, `.bsd_loop`, each checked against `tcpdump -y DLT` on savefiles (`src/testdata/link_oracle.zig`), refusals included (`ether host`, `multicast`, `vlan`; `arp` on NULL/LOOP). `Link.dlt` / `Link.fromDlt` name the savefile link types (1, 113, 276, 101, 0, 108). DLT_LINUX_SLL2: libpcap's `any` device offers both SLL (the default) and SLL2, and `tcpdump` 4.99.6 captures `-i any` as SLL2, so it is built (header 20 bytes, protocol first, `arp` allowed). DLT_NULL: the family word is in the capturing host's byte order, i.e. the FILE's (`Options.null_byte_order`, default this host's; `pcap.Reader.byteOrder()` gives the file's), compared as libpcap does for a savefile: `ip` is AF 2, `ip6` is 24, 28 or 30 (NetBSD/OpenBSD, FreeBSD, macOS), not Linux's 10.

## Threat model / out of scope


**Linux-only by design** — no BSD `/dev/bpf` path, no cross-platform abstraction attempted.
**Privilege-gated:** opening a capture/inject socket needs `CAP_NET_RAW`; without it `open` returns
a distinct `error.AccessDenied` rather than a generic failure (interface lookups like `ifaceByName`
are unprivileged and always available). This module is a **capability**, not a policy — it does not
itself restrict which interfaces/EtherTypes a caller may open; that access-control decision belongs
to the deployment (capability grant, network namespace, seccomp). The in-kernel BPF filter
(`setFilter`) reduces what userspace *sees*, it is not a security boundary against a co-resident
process with the same capability. Received frames are attacker-influenced wire data on a shared
L2 segment (spoofable source MAC, malformed lengths); the typed decode (`EthHeader.parse`,
`LinkAddr.fromSockaddr`, `arp.parseReply`) must reject malformed input without panicking — that
tolerant-parsing guarantee is the attack surface to audit, not the socket layer itself. The filter
compiler and the pcap reader take caller-supplied input; both are bounded (nesting depth, program
size, record lengths) and return typed errors. The `TPACKET_V3` ring (`ring.zig`) reads a mapping the kernel writes: every header from it is hostile input (see its header). Out of scope: `recvmmsg`
batching, a TX ring, IPv6 Neighbor Discovery (only ARP is implemented), pcapng blocks other than packets and interface descriptions.


**Limits and behaviour shared with libpcap, none of them unsafe to rely on once known:** (1) in the live ancillary `vlan` form a failed `vlan` test leaves the run-time shift at 4, so `vlan or ip` and `not vlan and ip` miss a plain untagged IPv4 frame on a live socket (`ip or vlan` does not): libpcap's own live programs do the same; (2) `mpls` and `pppoes` work alone only, anything written after them is `UnsupportedExpression`; (3) offline `ip and vlan` compiles here where libpcap refuses it; (4) a NULL savefile needs `Options.null_byte_order` when the file may come from the other kind of host; (5) `compile` on the deepest accepted inputs fits the documented 64 KiB stack, a smaller one (32 KiB) can overflow in a Debug build; (6) `pcap.writeRecord` takes the header's snaplen and refuses (`InvalidRecord`) a record longer than `max(snaplen, 262144)`, the bound `pcap.Reader` and libpcap's reader enforce (libpcap's `pcap_dump` and gopacket's `pcapgo` writer have no such check and write the file their own reader then rejects); (7) a filter past `max_insns` comparisons is `FilterTooComplex` while it is parsed, so a `Syntax` error after that point is reported as `FilterTooComplex`.

## Verification

Root-free tests (pure helpers, `sockaddr_ll` decode, BPF encoding, struct ABI sizes, fuzz-style never-panic checks) always run; the socket tests need `CAP_NET_RAW` and `SkipZigTest` without it. Under an unprivileged network namespace where root has the capability they all run, including open/filter/promisc and an inject→capture loopback round-trip on `lo`. Run: `scripts/modtest rawsock`, or `zig build test-rawsock` (add `-Doptimize=ReleaseFast` for the release check; `unshare -rn` prefix for the full socket path).

- **Filter compiler:** frame-by-frame against libpcap (`tcpdump -n -tt -r` verdicts over a synthetic frame corpus, recipe `tools/gen_filter_oracle.py`, which reproduces the corpus and the verdict lists byte for byte), including mixed `and`/`or` rows and long-jump rows (40 hosts, 25 `not host`, 30 `portrange`, 25 `ether host` terms); a live attach of a 120-term list (a `ja` stub present, the kernel accepts, passes only the last term's frame; netns lane). `run` is checked over libpcap's own `tcpdump -dd` programs. A compiled filter attached at open passes only its frame, and the kernel's verdict equals `run`'s.
- **Links, vlan, metadata:** `src/testdata/link_oracle.zig` and `vlan_live.zig` (`tcpdump -y DLT -r` and `tcpdump -i lo -dd`; recipe `tools/gen_link_oracle.py`); live vlan on `lo` (tag stays in the frame) and on a veth with a VLAN device (tag stripped), the latter in `interop-rawsock`; `inbound`/`outbound`/`ifindex` live on `lo`.
- **`run` and `validate`:** `run` against the KERNEL (`tools/kernel_semantics_probe.py`, frames on `lo` through `SO_ATTACH_FILTER`); a differential of seeded random kernel-valid programs between `run` and libpcap's `pcap_offline_filter` (`tools/gen_run_diff.py`, `tools/run_diff.c`, committed table `src/testdata/run_diff.zig`); a fuzz harness running random valid programs through `validate`, `run` and an independent model (`refRun`); `validate` against the kernel's attach-time verdicts (`tools/gen_validate_kernel.py`, table `src/testdata/validate_kernel.zig`, replayed), and 20,000 fresh seeded programs per run of `interop-rawsock` (by hand, `unshare -rn`; 2026-11-21: 20,000 agree, 5,573 accepted). `tools/protochain_probe.py` shows the kernel refusing libpcap's `protochain` programs (control program attaches).
- **Savefiles:** the pcap codec reproduces `tcpdump -w` files byte for byte (µs and ns) and decodes them to the times `tcpdump -tt -r` printed; pcapng files converted by Wireshark's `editcap -F pcapng` decode to the same frames and times as the classic files, and this writer's files are read by `tcpdump -r` and `capinfos` (recipe `tools/gen_pcapng_fixtures.py`); the pcapng reader's block checks are exercised by hand-built files in `src/pcapng.zig`.
- **Live:** `Options.timestamps` lands between send and receive on CLOCK_REALTIME; a fanout group splits round-robin and refuses a member with another mode or without DEFRAG; the V3 and V2 rings (frames, counters, teardown and re-setup, a second ring refused, crafted block headers). `interop-rawsock` (`unshare -rn zig build interop-rawsock`, by hand) asserts `ifaceByName`/`ifaceName`/`hwaddr`/`ipv4Addr`/`ipv4Netmask` against what `ip` configured and anchors `arp.buildRequest` against the kernel answering it (`-- --capture`).
- **Real-capture goldens:** a genuine ARP who-has/is-at exchange and Ethernet+IPv4 framing captured with `tcpdump` off a veth pair, each end in its own throwaway network namespace (`lo` never does ARP; a real L2 segment is required), anchoring real Ethernet framing and the ARP wire layout independently of `buildRequest`/`parseReply` agreeing with themselves.
- **Fuzz** (testkit's deterministic driver, `RAWSOCK_FUZZ=<runs>[,<first seed>]`, run in the ordinary test binary, each harness with a reach assertion): `rawsock-eth`, `rawsock-hwaddr`, `rawsock-arp`, `rawsock-filter` (well-formed program; `E and E` and `E or E` equal `E`; `not (E)` never accepts what `E` accepts; drives every link and both vlan forms), `rawsock-vlan-*`, `rawsock-run`, `rawsock-validate`, `rawsock-pcap`, `rawsock-pcapng` (records inside the input, termination, writer round trip), `rawsock-ring`, `rawsock-ring-seq` (a model of the cursor and `held`), `rawsock-ring2`, `rawsock-ring2-seq`. `rawsock-validate` checks no-panic only; agreement with the kernel is the replayed table.
- **Targets:** big-endian and 32-bit under qemu: `-Dtarget=mips-linux-musl -Dcpu=mips32+soft_float -fqemu` and `arm-linux-musleabihf -fqemu`; the capability-gated tests skip there.
- **Constant time:** n/a — raw sockets, no secret.
- **Audit:** the card's `**Audit:**` line is the current score, cumulative over the last whole-module mutation run and the delta runs after it. The live socket paths are not mutated.
- **Bench:** `zig build bench-rawsock` (`tools/bench.zig`, `tools/c_bench.c`, `tools/go_bench`, `tools/rust_bench`) against libpcap built from source, gopacket's `pcapgo` and the Rust `pcap-file` crate; the figures are the card's `**Performance:**` line.


## What is deliberately not done

- **Resolver-dependent primitives (host names, service names, `gateway`, `ip broadcast`/`multicast`):** these need the resolver, /etc/ethers or the interface netmask, i.e. system state a pure compiler must not read; the caller passes numbers (`UnsupportedExpression`).
- **`ip6 protochain` (and `ip protochain`): not built; the true reason.** libpcap compiles it to a loop with a `ja` that jumps BACKWARDS (`tcpdump -d 'ip6 protochain 6'`: `(018) ja 4`). The Linux kernel refuses that program at attach time, so it can never be a live filter (`tools/protochain_probe.py`, run with a control program that attaches: `ip6 protochain 6`, `ip6 protochain 44` and `ip protochain 6` all errno 22). libpcap's own USERSPACE interpreter does run it (`bpf_filter.c`: `pc += (bpf_int32)pc->k`, "we currently implement ip6 protochain with backward jumps"), so `pcap_offline_filter` filters a savefile with it. It is not built here because `filter.run` is loop-free by design (it terminates in `prog.len` steps, which is what lets it be total on hostile programs) and `validate` follows the kernel; a bounded unroll would not be libpcap's meaning.
- **Rejected filter keywords (each `UnsupportedExpression`):** `ifname`, `rnr`, `ruleset`, `reason`, `action`, `srnr`, `subrulenum` and the pflog words `link`/`on` (OpenBSD pflog only; libpcap: "supported only on PF linktype"); SS7/MTP (`fisu lssu msu sio opc dpc sls` and the `h*` forms), ATM (`lane oam oamf4 oamf4ec oamf4sc vpi vci connectmsg metaconnect sc ilmic callref bcc`), `decnet lat moprc mopdl sca iso clnp esis isis l1 l2 iih lsp snp csnp psnp stp ipx atalk aarp netbeui llc` and the `fddi`/`tr` qualifiers: no consumer and other link layers. The 802.11 words (`wlan`, `radio`, `type`, `subtype`, `dir`, `ra`, `ta`) are Backlog.
- **Rejected link types and capture sources:** DLT_PPP is built for savefiles (`Link.ppp`: `ip` is `ldh [2] == 0x21`, the IP header at 4; `tools/gen_ppp_oracle.py`, 52 rows against `tcpdump -y PPP -r`; MAC addresses, `vlan`, `multicast` and `broadcast` are refused as libpcap refuses them, `mpls` / `pppoes` / `pppoed` there are `UnsupportedExpression`), other PPP framings (PPP_WITH_DIR, HDLC, PPP over Ethernet DLTs) are not; a live Linux PPP device is DLT_LINUX_SLL in libpcap (`pcap-linux.c`, already built); every other link type, other operating systems' capture, rpcap, USB, Bluetooth, D-Bus and RDMA capture sources are separate subsystems and none is AF_PACKET.
- **A BPF optimiser:** the code is longer than libpcap's with the same verdicts on every tcpdump oracle row (known deviations: offline `ip and vlan` without an id, which libpcap refuses and this compiles; live `ip and vlan 5`, where libpcap's own program accepts nothing and ours accepts the frame it names); the kernel runs both within noise, and libpcap's shorter programs run faster in the same interpreter (`filter_run_lp` against `filter_run` in the bench). A real, measurable gain, not built.
- **pcapng Name Resolution, Interface Statistics, Decryption Secrets and custom blocks:** skipped by length, not interpreted.
- **IPv6 Neighbor Discovery codec:** not here; the sibling `l2disco.nd` (RFC 4861 messages, options, the ICMPv6 checksum, NS/RS builders) is the ND counterpart to `rawsock.arp`; a caller sends its frames with `Socket.sendRaw`. libpcap has no ND codec either.
- **`recvmmsg` batching, a TX ring, `PACKET_FANOUT` with the ring:** libpcap has none of them (it receives with `recvfrom` or a ring, sends with `send`); `Socket.joinFanout` covers fanout for the plain socket. No consumer is throughput-bound (the router-tool consumer captures a handful of LLDP/CDP/DHCP frames).
- **BSD `/dev/bpf` and other operating systems:** Linux-only is the documented AF_PACKET ceiling, permanent, not a gap to close.

## Backlog / deferred

- *BOUNCED (quiet-host):* **The IPC gap to the distro libpcap.so.** Same instruction count or fewer (0.93), 1.18× the cycles on `filter_run`; unprofiled. To chase it: `perf stat -e instructions:u,cycles:u,branch-misses:u,L1-icache-load-misses:u` for `bench-rawsock fixed filter_run 3000` against `FIXED_REPS=3000 .zig-cache/bench-rawsock/foreign_bench .zig-cache/bench-rawsock filter_run` (the distro-linked foreign binary), then `perf record -e cycles:u` and `perf annotate` of `exec` against `bpf_filter`; compare the dispatch `switch` layout (jump table or compare chain) and the `-Djcc-safe` effect. *Needs a quiet host: a measured claim needs a spread below the effect, and this host is shared.*

## Roadmap

- **802.11 savefiles and monitor mode.** Radiotap, the `wlan` qualifiers; no consumer, and no 802.11 capture to anchor a live path on this machine. Size: new link types, radiotap and wlan qualifiers in the filter compiler; needs an 802.11 capture to anchor on.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

- **Class A** — wire/interop format — other implementations must byte-agree with it.
- **Oracle EXTERNAL** — every wire or interop format the module speaks has bytes or verdicts from a foreign implementation or the kernel (below); the self-written residue is named.

**What the tests actually contain.** the `golden: real capture` tests in src/root.zig freeze a real ARP exchange and a real Ethernet/IPv4/ICMP frame captured with tcpdump off a veth pair in an unprivileged netns -- loopback cannot do ARP at all, which is why the pre-existing hand-computed fixture had never met a real L2 segment; since 2026-10-06 `arp.buildRequest` is anchored by the Linux kernel ANSWERING it (`unshare -rn zig build interop-rawsock -- --capture`: this module's `open`/`sendRaw`/`recv` on a veth pair, the kernel owning the target; request and the kernel's reply frozen in `src/testdata/kernel_arp.zig`, replayed by the "kernel ARP" test). The socket wrappers meet the kernel as a foreign peer only when that program runs (by hand); in the lane they stay self (loopback inject + capture of their own frames), which is the residue: those tests prove the wrappers move bytes, not that a foreign peer agrees. Anchored from outside since 2026-11-03: the filter compiler (100 expressions' frame verdicts from `tcpdump -r`, `run` over libpcap's own `-dd` programs; `tools/gen_filter_oracle.py`), classic pcap (two `tcpdump -w` files byte for byte) and pcapng (Wireshark `editcap` output decoded, this writer's output read by `tcpdump`/`capinfos`; `tools/gen_pcapng_fixtures.py`), the kernel's own filter verdict equal to `run` (netns lane), and the interface lookups against `ip` (`interop-rawsock`, by hand). Hand-computed only: `parseHwaddr`/`formatHwaddr` text forms and the `EthHeader` field edge cases (the header itself is also read off real captured frames).
